problem: Existing world models are visual-only; there is no formulation, benchmark or architecture for jointly predicting synchronized binaural audio and vision under low-level action control with physical consistency.
motivation: Real-world perception is multimodal, and audio gives spatial and temporal cues (including non-line-of-sight) that vision lacks. Embodied agents should anticipate the multisensory consequences of their actions, so a world model must keep audio and vision physically coupled. Naively adding audio to a visually pretrained model risks visual dominance suppressing audio learning.
key_idea: Build an action-conditioned audio-visual diffusion transformer (AV-CDiT) with shared attention, per-modality FFN experts and three-stage training (vision, then audio with frozen shared layers, then joint), trained on a new binaural AV benchmark (AVW-4k), and use it for lookahead planning in audio-visual navigation.
insight: Ablations show that removing modality experts or stagewise training leaves visual fidelity nearly unchanged but hurts audio fidelity and physical consistency. For example, AV-Lag error rises from 1.218 to about 1.61 and SSIM falls from 0.547 to 0.485. So the benefit lies in the auditory pathway and cross-modal coupling. Unfreezing all layers in stage 2 diverged, so freezing the shared attention is needed to avoid forgetting visual priors. Oracle world-model results (SPL 51-52) show that better rollout quality would give more navigation gain.
method: Problem formulation: Audio-Visual World Model as a POMDP with observations {RGB 128x128, 0.15 s binaural audio} and low-level actions; predicts o_{t+Δt} from an m-frame context, relative motion (displacement and heading change) and Δt (skip-step prediction, following NWM).

AVW-4k dataset: about 30 h, 4,500 trajectories, 76 Matterport3D scenes in SoundSpaces 2.0, a stationary looping telephone-ring source, three motion patterns (approaching, receding, independent), and 4 actions (forward 0.15 m, turn ±10°, stop). Train/val/test ratio is 6:1:2 with disjoint scenes.

AV-CDiT backbone: frozen SD-VAE for vision and a SoundStream tokenizer (trained on AVW-4k) for audio; separate adaptors project into a shared space; visual and audio tokens are concatenated, noised (DDPM, epsilon-prediction plus learned covariance with L_vb), and denoised through CDiT blocks with shared self-attention, cross-attention to context frames and AdaLN conditioning on action, Δt and diffusion timestep.
Modality experts: the feed-forward layer of each block is split into a visual expert and an auditory expert applied to the respective token groups, then concatenated, preventing visual dominance.

Three-stage training: (1) vision-only fine-tuning of shared attention, visual expert, adaptor and head, initialized from pretrained NWM; (2) audio-only tuning of the auditory expert, adaptor and head with everything else frozen; (3) end-to-end joint audio-visual fine-tuning.

Reward-aware planning: an AV-CDiT variant with an auxiliary progress-reward token (reduction in geodesic distance to the source). An AV-Nav policy samples n=2 candidate actions, AVWM rolls out k steps, and beam search (width B) scores branches by discounted predicted reward plus the policy value; the first action is executed.

setting.backbone: AV-CDiT (CDiT-base, initialized from pretrained NWM, fine-tuned) with frozen SD-VAE and SoundStream tokenizer; planning uses a pretrained AV-Nav (SoundSpaces) policy

results: AV-CDiT matches the visual-only NWM on LPIPS (0.382) and DreamSim (0.255 vs 0.258) while adding audio. It clearly beats DIAMOND/NWM+AudioLDM and AVDiT+action on ILD (2.471), AV-Lag (1.218) and AV-Corr (0.194). As a planner it lifts the AV-Nav agent's SPL from 45.08 to 47.38 and cuts actions from 332.8 to 317.2 (B=3, k=5); the oracle world model reaches SPL 51.98.
limitations: Benchmark is synthetic, indoor, and uses a single stationary source with a fixed ringtone; the mixed-source variant is only a supplementary test, and moving sources and real-world audio are not covered.
Navigation gains are modest (SPL +2.3) and depend on beam width and rollout length; there is a large gap to the oracle world model, so rollout quality still limits planning.
Consistency metrics (ILD, AV-Lag, AV-Corr) are proxies; audio LSD is slightly worse than AVDiT+action; some ablation differences in vision are tiny and single-scene-set.
